data.narrative: Adopted the reviewer/decider role for AI agents: mapped the codebase and extension points before prompting, trust-but-verified six claims with real commands, disproved the intentional wrong-claim card, diagnosed its failure mode, and recorded the calibration in artifacts.

dimension_scores.observation: Listed concrete preparation steps (data model, routing/error patterns, product constraints) before any prompt and grounded them in the actual fork schema.
dimension_scores.evidence: codebase-summary.md maps User/Link/ClickEvent and extension points; negative claim 'no Team tables' verified against models.py.

dimension_scores.observation: Ran 6 spot-check commands against 6 factual claims, recorded all results, and identified the negative-claim pattern as highest-risk.
dimension_scores.evidence: trust-audit.md: 6/6 MATCH, no discrepancies, calibration notes on which claims to spot-check.

dimension_scores.observation: Precisely identified the wrong claim, wrote a corrected evidence-constrained prompt, and correctly classified the cause as insufficient context rather than hallucination or ambiguous code.
dimension_scores.evidence: fix-record.md with the 3-way failure-mode analysis and the 'fixable with a better prompt vs must verify via commands' conclusion.

dimension_scores.observation: Chose task-by-task with reasoning tied to error-discovery-cost asymmetry and reviewability of small diffs.
dimension_scores.evidence: decisions.module_01.delegation_strategy = B with cost asymmetry rationale.

dimension_scores.observation: Applied the 80/20 rule consistently: verified the 20% (edge cases, negative claims, integration reality) rather than accepting the 80% prototype.
dimension_scores.evidence: Every agent claim verified via commands or targeted file lookups, not accepted on confidence.

dimension_scores.observation: Clear evidence trail and calibration, but no formal postmortem-style artifact with timeline and owner-backed remediations for the agent failure.
dimension_scores.evidence: fix-record.md is thorough but focused on the correction rather than a full incident writeup.

strengths: Verified negative claims (the highest-risk agent statements) with commands.
Correctly diagnosed the wrong claim as a context failure and showed why better prompts fix that class.
Grounded all extension points in the real schema, preventing the Capable Intern from inventing tables.
growth_areas: Add a structured postmortem artifact for agent-failure incidents with owner-backed follow-ups.
Expand spot-check cadence to include the config layer and queue wiring in future summaries.
data.recommendation: Maintain the trust-audit as a living file, and in later modules run spot-checks on claims that will change how features are built (schema and dependency claims).

public_evidence.student_action: Verified the agent's codebase summary with 6 spot-check commands and disproved the intentional wrong-claim card (no application files) with a root listing, source count, and a full pytest run.
public_evidence.technical_detail: trust-audit.md records claim/command/result for C1-C6; BREAK section records observed output (api/, 34 files, 76 tests exit 0) and corrected statement.
public_evidence.proof: 6/6 claims MATCH; pytest 76 tests exit 0; corrected statement recorded.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows a candidate who converts agent confidence into verified facts and keeps a running calibration file.
